statement: Let $f(x) = 2x - 3$. For what value of $k$ is $f(f(f(k))) = 13$?

choices.misconception: I thought applying f three times would cube each part of the rule, so I solved 8k - 27 = 13 and got k = 5.
I undid f by halving and then adding 3 each time, getting 13, 9.5, 7.75 and 6.875, but to undo f I should add 3 first and then halve.
I applied f only once and solved 2k - 3 = 13 to get k = 8, but the equation has f used three times.

hints: Either build a formula for $f(f(f(x)))$ or work backward from $13$ one step at a time.
To undo $f$, reverse its steps in reverse order: add $3$, then divide by $2$.
Working backward from $13$: $13 \to 8 \to 5.5 \to \ldots$, one more step to go.

solutions.elegant: Undo $f$ three times. The inverse of $f$ is $f^{-1}(y) = \frac{y + 3}{2}$, so $13 \to 8 \to 5.5 \to 4.25$. Check: $f(4.25) = 5.5$, $f(5.5) = 8$ and $f(8) = 13$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
